summary_en: Nihon M&A Center Holdings will acquire shares in AI Brain Partners (established September 2025) and complete its acquisition through simplified share exchange. AIBP specializes in supporting companies' in-house AI implementation and organizational transformation across four business lines. The acquisition aims to enhance group productivity through AI-driven business process optimization and expand customer value offerings with AI adoption support during M&A sourcing and post-merger integration phases.
title_en: Notice Regarding Share Acquisition and Full Subsidiary Status of AI Brain Partners Co., Ltd. through Simplified Share Exchange
translation_en_brief:
Nihon M&A Center Holdings announced on September 18, 2026, that its board of directors has decided to acquire shares in AI Brain Partners Co., Ltd. (AIBP), followed by a simplified share exchange to make AIBP a wholly owned subsidiary. AIBP was established in September 2025 and operates four business lines: AI and BPO product development support, company-wide AI transformation consulting, AI advisory and executive guidance, and AI training programs. The company's core strength lies in its execution capability to implement AI agents and redesign operating models, with experience across major trading companies, corporations, and government agencies.

The acquisition is positioned as a solution to the group's primary management challenge during its "second founding" phase. Nihon M&A Center recognizes that deploying AI tools alone does not improve organizational productivity; rather, the group must redesign existing business processes and enable employees to collaborate with AI. AIBP's deep expertise in business requirement definition, implementation, and continuous improvement aligns with the group's need for specialized human capital in this domain.

The transaction is expected to generate synergies across two dimensions. First, the group aims to apply AIBP's knowledge to improve productivity throughout the transaction lifecycle, from engagement through completion, enabling consultants to concentrate on high-value-added activities such as client dialogue and proposals. Second, the group plans to expand its customer value proposition by providing AI adoption and implementation support during both the M&A sourcing and post-merger integration phases. As corporate clients increasingly address AI utilization within the context of business succession and growth strategy, this expanded service offering is anticipated to strengthen the group's competitive positioning.
